title: Advancing Graph Foundation Models: A Data-Centric Perspective

problem.claim: Graph foundation models rely on large-scale pre-training over extensive and diverse graph data to support zero-shot generalization across domains and tasks.

gap.claim: Existing graph foundation models face extreme pre-training time costs and redundancy and noise in their pre-training data.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces a data-centric approach that optimizes pre-training data, represented as a set of subgraphs, to improve efficiency while maintaining robust downstream performance.

DCGFM is a plug-and-play data-pruning approach with model-agnostic hard pruning based on semantic and structural informativity and model-aware soft pruning based on per-epoch loss values with gradient rescaling.
The authors state that code and data are available.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on representative graph foundation model backbones are reported to demonstrate DCGFM's efficiency and effectiveness.
The authors report that DCGFM achieves better performance using only 30% of the pre-training data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph foundation models have emerged as an important graph machine learning topic and show zero-shot generalization through large-scale pre-training.
Existing pre-training approaches are limited by high time costs and redundant or noisy data.
The paper proposes a data-centric graph foundation model approach and introduces DCGFM to prune redundant and less informative subgraphs.
DCGFM combines semantic- and structure-aware hard pruning with model-aware soft pruning using dynamic per-epoch pruning and gradient rescaling.
The authors report efficiency and effectiveness across representative backbones, including better performance with 30% of the pre-training data, and provide code and data.

source_observation.claim: The approach reduces pre-training data to 30% while the authors report better performance.

interpretation.claim: Removing redundant or less informative training units may improve both computational efficiency and model effectiveness.

application.claim: For large-scale graph pre-training, evaluate data-pruning strategies that combine domain or structure-aware scoring with model-aware dynamic selection.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported gains generalize beyond the evaluated representative backbones, tasks, or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated datasets, downstream tasks, metrics, or baseline configurations.
The abstract does not report the computational savings, absolute performance values, or statistical variation.
The abstract does not provide details of the informativity scores, pruning schedules, or gradient rescaling formulation.
